Best dates: Monday Nov 23 to Friday Nov 27 (4 nights)

Monday out, Black Friday back is the cheapest clean pattern that still covers Thanksgiving dinner, and it's the exact date pair every price on this page was checked against. Wednesday Nov 25 departures and Sunday Nov 29 returns carry the steepest premiums of the week. Want 5 nights? Add Sunday Nov 22 on the front end.

Primary: Mon 11/23 → Fri 11/27All prices below verified for this pair
5-night option: Sun 11/22 → Fri 11/27Adds a night at low cost
Avoid: Wed 11/25 out, Sun 11/29 backThe two priciest travel days

How to use this guide: the homes below are real, live listings confirmed bookable for these dates, but treat them as examples of what each destination offers at this budget. The move is to pick the destination first on the family call, then immediately lock the best available house that same week; Thanksgiving-week inventory moves fast.

On the ground

  • Two minivans at SAN: ~$1,100-1,600 for the stay. Book by early fall.
  • Thanksgiving dinner: cook at the house, or go out: George's at the Cove ocean-view dinner ~$1,000 for the group, Hotel Del's blowout buffet ~$2,900.
  • Activities: San Diego Zoo (~$790 group, under-3s free), Balboa Park (mostly free), Coronado + holiday ice rink at Hotel Del, 1-hr harbor cruise (~$400 group, perfect nap-length), La Jolla sea lions (free), Torrey Pines walk.
Bottom lineChoose San Diego if you want the smoothest all-family logistics with real warmth: nonstops for every flying family, a free drive for the LA four, and the best toddler-activity lineup of any option.

On the ground

  • Passports: all 13 need valid passport books, including both babies (infant passports: both parents apply in person, ~$135, 4-6 weeks). Start now if any are missing.
  • Transport: skip rental cars; the villas arrange drivers. Airport transfers ~$300-460 each way for the group, day-trip van + driver ~$180-300/day. Use the toll highway (about 90 scenic minutes). Budget ~$1,200-1,800 total.
  • Thanksgiving: cook it in the villa kitchens (Villa Bonita's is a full cooking-school kitchen); turkeys are easy to source in Mexico in late November.
  • Activities: Tepozteco pyramid hike + the Wednesday/Sunday market, Las Estacas natural spring river (~$30/adult, toddler-friendly shallows), Teotihuacán day trip (~$5 entry), Xochimilco boats (~$80 for the whole group), in-villa cooking class with Chef Ana.
Bottom lineChoose Mexico if the trip should feel like a real getaway: a villa with daily housekeeping and breakfast made for you, in a sunny mountain town, with the best food story of any option. The lift: passports for all 13 including two babies, and the longest travel day for the Sun Valley crew.

On the ground

  • Two minivans at Logan: ~$1,100-1,500. No off-season Cape bridge traffic.
  • Thanksgiving dinner: cook at the house, or grab a heat-and-serve turkey package (~$300-450), or do the "Story of Thanksgiving" dinner AT Plimoth Patuxet on Thanksgiving night (~$1,360 group incl. 2 days of museum admission).
  • Activities: Plimoth Patuxet + Mayflower II (~$46/adult heritage pass), Edaville Christmas-lights train (opens Thanksgiving weekend, under-2s free), Gardens Aglow in Sandwich (opens Nov 27, $28/adult), New England Aquarium, World's End Hingham and the 1928 Paragon Carousel in Hull, both minutes from Cohasset.
  • Timing note: Plymouth's Thanksgiving parade is Sat Nov 21; arrive that Saturday to catch it.
Bottom lineChoose Cohasset if the theme beats the tan: real-deal Plymouth Thanksgiving, holiday lights kicking off, the cheapest houses in the guide, and zero travel for the Boston three. The costs: cold weather, 4:15 sunsets, and the two western families carry the longest flights.

On the ground

  • Two minivans at SJU: ~$1,100-1,600 for the week. US licenses, US road rules.
  • Thanksgiving dinner: cook at the villa (all four have full kitchens); Luquillo's famous food kioskos cover the other nights cheaply.
  • Activities: El Yunque rainforest (free entry, stroller-friendly El Portal paths), Luquillo's calm lifeguarded beach + famous food kioskos, Old San Juan forts (kids free, kite-flying lawn), bio bay by electric boat at La Parguera (all ages) or kayak at Fajardo (6+ only), Carabalí rainforest hayrides (all ages).
  • Season note: hurricane season formally ends Nov 30 but actual late-November risk is very low; trip insurance is still smart.
Bottom lineChoose Puerto Rico if warm, swimmable ocean is non-negotiable and Mexico's passport lift kills that option. It delivers 84° with domestic-travel simplicity, but it's the most expensive overall and the toughest travel day for Boise and LA.

How to decide

No option wins everything, so the family call really needs to settle one question: is this trip about ease, warmth, the villa experience, or the theme? Pick the destination first; the housing list above proves each one has multiple great, in-budget homes still open, and we lock the best one the same week.

Cheapest + easiest travel: Las Vegas (~$5,850)

Cheapest flights, shortest travel for 3 of 4 families, and a 417-review house with a free heated pool at $3,796. The tradeoff is vibe: it's Vegas, in jackets.

Most on-theme: Cohasset (~$6,050)

Plymouth itself, holiday lights opening weekend, a 4.98-star house at $3,191, zero travel for the Boston crew. Cold and dark by 4:15pm.

Sunniest sure thing: Scottsdale (~$7,350)

72° and dry-season sun, nonstops from every city, a 4.98-star heated-pool house at $4,266, and toddler gold in the railroad park and ZooLights. Middle of the pack on flights.

Best all-around family trip: San Diego (~$7,900)

Warm, sunny, nonstops for everyone who flies, a free drive for the LA four, and the strongest toddler lineup (Zoo, Balboa Park, beaches). The value house brings it to ~$6,400.

Best experience per dollar: Mexico (~$8,250)

A chef's villa with daily maid service and homemade breakfast for $2,741 total, in a mountain town in the sun. The lift: passports for all 13 (including two babies) and the Sun Valley crew's longest travel day.

Warmest, passport-free: Puerto Rico (~$10,500)

83° ocean in late November, no documents needed. Costs the most and gives the Sun Valley family a 9-13 hour journey with a lap infant.

Next steps, whatever gets picked

  • Decide the destination by mid-August. The confirmed homes above won't all last; Thanksgiving week books early.
  • Book the house immediately after the call. Most of the featured homes have free cancellation windows, so locking one in early is low-risk.
  • Book flights by early September. Thanksgiving fares bottom out late August to mid September; the Boise legs are the most volatile and go first.
  • If Mexico: confirm all 13 passports today; infant passports take 4-6 weeks plus an in-person appointment with both parents.
  • Sun Valley family: decide SUN vs the 2.5-hr drive to Boise when booking; Boise is much cheaper for everywhere except Mexico City.
  • Reserve two minivans early; holiday-week family vehicles sell out at every airport on this list.
